bias_targets.methodology: Prospective scenario analysis and theoretical modeling of multi-agent systems (MAS) to evaluate how proxy variables (e.g., postal codes, employment forms) can lead to implicit social scoring, systemic marginalization, and discriminatory resource allocation against low-income and vulnerable populations.

Theoretical scenario-based evaluation exploring how seemingly neutral administrative data in AI welfare systems can act as proxies for protected attributes like ethnicity or migrant background, resulting in algorithmic discrimination.

Theoretically evaluated in the context of proxy discrimination, demonstrating how multi-agent welfare systems might inadvertently reconstruct and discriminate based on protected characteristics like gender despite explicit removal of such variables.
Theoretically identified alongside gender and ethnicity as a protected attribute vulnerable to indirect algorithmic proxy discrimination in decentralized social welfare evaluations.
